title: Indian Street Food Brand Puchkaman Makes Global Debut With First Toronto Location
excerpt: The Kolkata-born QSR chain, backed by Wow! Momo co-founder, opens at Scarborough's Danforth Avenue as Indian food brands accelerate their North American expansion.
body:
• Puchkaman, India's fast-growing pani puri and street-food chain, has opened its first international outlet at 3315 Danforth Avenue in Scarborough, Toronto.
  • The brand, founded in 2018, operates multiple outlets across India including Kolkata, Bangalore, and Siliguri, with mentorship from Wow! Momo co-founder Binod Kumar Homagai.
  • The Toronto launch positions Puchkaman among a growing wave of Indian food chains entering the Canadian market, reflecting surging demand for authentic Indian flavors abroad.
  • Canada's Indian diaspora, now exceeding 1.8 million, has created a thriving market for Indian QSR brands seeking international expansion.

Puchkaman, one of India's fastest-growing street-food brands, has officially opened its first international restaurant in Toronto's Scarborough neighborhood, marking a significant step in the chain's global expansion plans.

The new outlet at 3315 Danforth Avenue represents the brand's debut outside India, bringing its signature pani puri and street snacks to one of North America's most diverse food markets.

From Kolkata's Lanes to Canada's Largest City

Founded in 2018 by Sujoy Bose and Sk Saikat, Puchkaman was built on a straightforward vision: transform India's beloved street-food staple — pani puri, known as puchka in eastern India — into a hygienic, standardized quick-service restaurant format.

The brand combines authentic flavors with modern food-safety practices and contemporary presentation, a formula that has fueled its rapid expansion across India. Puchkaman now operates outlets in Kolkata, Bangalore, Siliguri, Bardhaman, Bolpur, Singur, South 24 Parganas, and Sikkim, with additional locations in the pipeline.

"This is more than a store opening — it is the global debut of India's street-food culture."

— Puchkaman

In its early days, the founders received support from Jayeeta Mitra, who helped shape the brand's foundation and growth trajectory. The chain's rapid and structured expansion has been guided by the mentorship and investment of Binod Kumar Homagai, co-founder of Wow! Momo, one of India's most successful QSR chains.

Why Toronto, Why Now

Toronto's selection as Puchkaman's first international market is no accident. The Greater Toronto Area is home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities outside South Asia, with over 800,000 people of Indian origin. The city has long been a proving ground for South Asian food concepts, from fine dining to fast casual.

The Scarborough location on Danforth Avenue places Puchkaman in a corridor already popular with South Asian diners and families, offering easy access to a built-in customer base hungry for authentic Indian street food.

A Wave of Indian Food Brands Heading North

Puchkaman's Toronto launch is part of a broader trend of Indian restaurant brands expanding into Canada. Chalu Apna Desi Chinese, the Indian-Chinese chain with over 200 outlets across India, opened its first Canadian location in Ontario in 2024 and has announced plans for 25 outlets nationwide. ROOH, a health-conscious Indian fine-dining concept with roots in San Francisco, opened on Toronto's College Street in 2025, earning recognition alongside its Michelin Guide-listed sister restaurant Bar Goa.

Quebec-based SpiceBros, which blends Indian flavors with Western formats through items like butter chicken poutine and Frankie rolls, recently expanded from its seven Quebec locations into the Toronto market. UK-based chaiiwala, founded in 1927 in New Delhi, has also been growing its footprint in the Greater Toronto Area.

Street Food Goes Global

The international expansion of Indian street-food brands represents a shift in how Indian cuisine is consumed globally. For decades, Indian restaurants abroad typically meant sit-down dining with standardized menus of butter chicken and naan. The new wave emphasizes regional specialties, quick-service formats, and the kind of street-food experience that has long been central to how Indians actually eat.

Puchkaman's franchise-driven model, proven across Indian cities of varying sizes, is designed to scale internationally. The brand's focus on pani puri — a snack with passionate devotees across every Indian state — gives it a distinctive identity in a crowded market.

What's Next

While Puchkaman has not publicly announced a timeline for additional Canadian locations, its franchise model and the growing appetite for Indian QSR concepts in North America suggest further expansion is likely. For Toronto's sizable Indian community, the arrival of a dedicated puchka chain may fill a gap that no amount of fine dining or fusion restaurants has managed to address.
